text:
kevin: quick sanity check — noticed Authorization header disappears after a 307 redirect when hitting our kotlin client. followRedirects is true. anyone seen this before?

maria: yep, okHttp will drop auth on cross-host redirects by default. are you adding the header in a normal interceptor or network interceptor?

kevin: addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor(...)) — simple one that sets header on request. example:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .followRedirects(true)
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor(tokenProvider))
  .build()
```
but when the server replies 307 -> different-host, the second request has no Authorization.

maria: right — addInterceptor runs before redirects are resolved. OkHttp clears sensitive headers for cross-host redirects. two quick fixes:
- move auth to addNetworkInterceptor so it runs on network requests after redirect resolution
- or implement an Authenticator to respond to 401s / reapply token when redirected

samir: also watch for this subtlety: if you move it to network interceptor, you may re-send the token on internal redirects to S3/third-party. if that's a concern, you can check `request.url.host` against allowed hosts before attaching header.

kevin: good call. does anyone know if addNetworkInterceptor runs before or after the redirect logic? want to be sure it actually sees the redirected URL.

maria: network interceptors see the fully resolved network request (including redirects), so you'll get the final host. interceptors (non-network) see the original user request.

olga: unrelated but FYI — saw another flaky failure: Jackson deserializing streaming responses intermittently with 400-ish bytes errors; turned out to be charset mismatch + BOM from upstream. we had `Content-Type: application/json` (no charset) but body started with UTF-8 BOM, and Kotlin String conversion choked. adding `.body?.source().readUtf8()` vs `.string()` differences surfaced it.

kevin: ack — we should normalize reading logic in our streaming helper. any simple rugged approach?

olga: safest: use response.body?.source().readString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8) (explicit charset) or strip BOM before handing to Jackson. also make sure Jackson's Kotlin module is configured for non-null defaults.

samir: one more gotcha we hit in a shaded fatjar: if you relocate packages incorrectly you can end up with two copies of jackson-kotlin-module classes at runtime -> weird NoSuchMethodError during deserialize. verify the jar has only one jackson-databind / kotlin-module and relocated packages if shading.

kevin: ugh, we do ship a shaded agent plugin — good reminder. i'll run `jar tf` on the artifact and grep for com/fasterxml to confirm.

maria: summary action items:
- kevin: try moving AuthInterceptor to network interceptor and gate by host OR implement Authenticator (your call)
- olga: add BOM-stripping utility + explicit UTF-8 reads to streaming helper
- samir: validate shaded jars for duplicate jackson packages and add check to CI

kevin: thanks — i'll send a short PR for the interceptor change and add a test for redirect host matching. pinging @ci-bot to run the shaded-jar scan on next build? :pray:

ci-bot: scheduled: shaded-jar-scan will run on build/8342, report back in ~5m. :gear:
